**Section 6.4 --- Excess Generation**

Buyer shall accept and pay for all Energy delivered by Seller in excess of the Minimum Annual Delivery up to one hundred fifteen percent (115%) of the Expected Annual Generation for the applicable Contract Year. For Energy delivered in excess of 115% of the Expected Annual Generation in any Contract Year, Buyer may, in its sole discretion, curtail generation at the Facility without obligation to compensate Seller for any such Curtailed Energy. Seller shall comply promptly with any curtailment instruction issued by Buyer pursuant to this Section 6.4.

**Section 6.5 --- Metering**

Metering of all Energy delivered at the Delivery Point shall be performed using revenue-grade meters conforming to ERCOT metering requirements and applicable industry standards. Seller shall own, procure, install, calibrate, and maintain all revenue meters at the Delivery Point at Seller\'s sole cost and expense. Buyer shall have the right, at Buyer\'s sole cost and expense, to install, own, and maintain one or more check meters at or near the Delivery Point for verification purposes. All revenue meters shall be tested and calibrated at least annually, or more frequently upon the reasonable request of either Party. If any meter is found to have an error in excess of plus or minus one-half of one percent (±0.5%), the metering data shall be retroactively adjusted to correct the error for the lesser of (a) the period during which the error existed or (b) twelve (12) months prior to the discovery of the error. The cost of any retroactive adjustment shall be borne by Seller if the error resulted in under-measurement of Energy delivered.

**Section 6.6 --- Scheduling**

Seller shall register and maintain registration of the Facility as a Generation Resource in ERCOT in accordance with the ERCOT Protocols. Seller shall submit generation schedules and resource plans to ERCOT as required by the ERCOT Protocols. In addition, Seller shall provide Buyer with day-ahead generation forecasts by 06:00 Central Prevailing Time on each day and shall provide updated real-time generation forecasts as conditions change materially, in each case using commercially reasonable forecasting methods and the Facility\'s historical generation data.

**Section 6.7 --- Record Keeping**

Seller shall maintain complete and accurate records of all generation data, solar irradiance data from on-site pyranometers and weather stations, BESS charge and discharge logs, Availability records, meter data, maintenance records, curtailment events, and all other records reasonably necessary to verify Seller\'s performance under this Agreement. All such records shall be maintained for a period of not less than five (5) years following the period to which they relate. Buyer shall have the right, upon not less than thirty (30) days\' prior written notice, to audit and inspect Seller\'s records at reasonable times during normal business hours at Seller\'s offices.

**Section 6.8 --- Degradation Adjustment**

The Parties acknowledge that the solar photovoltaic modules comprising the Facility will experience performance degradation over time due to normal aging, weathering, and operational factors. To account for such degradation, the Minimum Annual Delivery and the Expected Annual Generation shall each be adjusted downward by the Degradation Rate of zero and fifty-hundredths percent (0.50%) per Contract Year, compounding annually, beginning in Contract Year 2. The adjusted Minimum Annual Delivery for each Contract Year shall be calculated as follows:

> Minimum Annual Delivery (Year N) = 490,000 MWh × (1 -- 0.005)\^(N--1)

By way of illustration:

> • Contract Year 1: 490,000 MWh (no adjustment)
>
> • Contract Year 2: 490,000 × (1 -- 0.005)\^1 = 487,550 MWh
>
> • Contract Year 5: 490,000 × (1 -- 0.005)\^4 = approximately 480,267 MWh
>
> • Contract Year 10: 490,000 × (1 -- 0.005)\^9 = approximately 468,367 MWh
>
> • Contract Year 15: 490,000 × (1 -- 0.005)\^14 = approximately 456,715 MWh
>
> • Contract Year 20: 490,000 × (1 -- 0.005)\^19 = approximately 445,537 MWh

The Degradation Rate is a fixed rate established by the Parties as of the Amended and Restated Date and shall not be adjusted, trued up, or recalculated based on actual measured degradation of the solar modules or any other component of the Facility at any time during the Delivery Term. The Degradation Rate is applied uniformly across all Contract Years and is not intended to replicate actual module degradation curves, which may vary based on environmental conditions, module technology, and other factors.

**[ARTICLE 7 --- CURTAILMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- Buyer Economic Curtailment**

Buyer may instruct Seller to curtail, reduce, or cease generation from the Facility at any time for economic reasons, including without limitation when the market price of Energy at Buyer\'s Load Zone or the Delivery Point is below the Contract Price or is negative. Seller shall comply with Buyer\'s curtailment instructions as promptly as practicable. Buyer shall not be required to compensate Seller for Curtailed Energy up to five percent (5%) of the Expected Annual Generation per Contract Year (the \"Free Curtailment Allowance\"). For Contract Year 1, the Free Curtailment Allowance equals five percent (5%) of 612,500 MWh, or 30,625 MWh (as adjusted for degradation pursuant to Section 6.8 in subsequent Contract Years). For any Curtailed Energy in excess of the Free Curtailment Allowance in any Contract Year, Buyer shall pay Seller the Contract Price applicable to such Contract Year for each MWh of Deemed Generated Energy curtailed in excess of the Free Curtailment Allowance.

**Section 7.2 --- System/Reliability Curtailment (ERCOT-Directed)**

In the event of a Curtailment Order by ERCOT or a Transmission Service Provider directing the Facility to reduce or cease generation for system reliability, transmission constraint management, or other grid management reasons, such curtailment shall be treated as an event of Force Majeure under Article 17, and Seller shall be excused from its delivery obligations for the period of such Curtailment Order; provided, however, that the Force Majeure treatment of Curtailment Orders shall apply only for the first five hundred (500) hours of Curtailment Orders in any Contract Year (the \"System Curtailment Threshold\"). For any hours of Curtailment Orders in excess of the System Curtailment Threshold in any Contract Year, the following provisions shall apply:

> \(a\) Such excess hours shall not be treated as Force Majeure under Article 17 or any other provision of this Agreement;
>
> \(b\) The Curtailed Energy associated with such excess hours shall not be excluded from the calculation of Seller\'s actual deliveries for purposes of determining whether Seller has met the Minimum Annual Delivery for such Contract Year; that is, the Deemed Generated Energy for such excess curtailment hours shall be deemed to have been required to be delivered by Seller and shall count as a shortfall against the Minimum Annual Delivery; and
>
> \(c\) Seller shall bear the full risk of lost revenue for such excess curtailment hours, and neither Buyer nor ERCOT shall have any obligation to compensate Seller for any Curtailed Energy or lost revenue arising during excess curtailment hours.

For the avoidance of doubt, if Seller\'s actual deliveries to the Delivery Point in any Contract Year, after accounting for the inclusion of Curtailed Energy during excess curtailment hours (i.e., hours in excess of the System Curtailment Threshold) as undelivered Energy, fall below the Minimum Annual Delivery for such Contract Year, Seller shall be liable for Shortfall Liquidated Damages under Section 6.3. The Parties acknowledge that the System Curtailment Threshold is a negotiated allocation of curtailment risk and that the five hundred (500)-hour threshold reflects the Parties\' shared assumption regarding the anticipated frequency and duration of ERCOT-directed curtailment at the Delivery Point.

**Section 7.3 --- BESS Dispatch Rights**

\(a\) **Peak Hours (Buyer Exclusive).** During Peak Hours (Hour Beginning 14:00 through Hour Beginning 19:00, Central Prevailing Time, during the months of June, July, August, and September of each calendar year), Buyer shall have the exclusive right to direct the charging and discharging of the BESS. Seller shall comply with Buyer\'s dispatch instructions during Peak Hours, subject to the physical and technical limitations of the BESS, including the BESS\'s state of charge, thermal constraints, and any manufacturer-specified operating limitations. During Peak Hours, Seller shall not dispatch the BESS for Ancillary Services or any other purpose without Buyer\'s prior written consent.

\(b\) **Non-Peak Hours (Shared Rights).** During all Non-Peak Hours, dispatch rights with respect to the BESS shall be shared between the Parties. Seller shall have the right to utilize the BESS for the provision of Ancillary Services to ERCOT during Non-Peak Hours; provided, however, that:

> \(i\) Such use does not reduce the Availability of the BESS below ninety percent (90%) measured on a rolling thirty (30)-Day basis; and
>
> \(ii\) Seller provides Buyer with reasonable advance notice (not less than two (2) hours) of any intended Ancillary Services dispatch, including the anticipated duration and power level of such dispatch.

\(c\) **Ancillary Services Revenue Sharing.** Net revenue derived from the provision of Ancillary Services by the BESS during Non-Peak Hours shall be allocated sixty percent (60%) to Seller and forty percent (40%) to Buyer. For purposes of this Section 7.3(c), \"net revenue\" means gross revenue received from ERCOT for Ancillary Services less any direct costs, charges, or penalties assessed by ERCOT in connection with the provision of such Ancillary Services. Seller shall provide Buyer with a detailed quarterly accounting of all Ancillary Services revenue and costs within thirty (30) days following the end of each calendar quarter, and Buyer\'s share of net revenue shall be credited on Seller\'s next monthly invoice following such quarterly accounting.

\(d\) **Priority.** In the event of a conflict between Buyer\'s dispatch instructions and Seller\'s Ancillary Services activities during Non-Peak Hours, Buyer\'s dispatch instructions shall take priority, and Seller shall promptly curtail or modify its Ancillary Services activities to comply with Buyer\'s instructions.

\(e\) **BESS State of Charge.** Seller shall ensure that the BESS is charged to no less than eighty percent (80%) of its rated energy capacity (i.e., no less than 240 MWh) by Hour Beginning 13:00 Central Prevailing Time on each day during the months of June, July, August, and September, to enable Buyer\'s exercise of its exclusive dispatch rights during Peak Hours. Seller shall manage the charging of the BESS from the solar facility and/or the grid to ensure compliance with this requirement.

**Section 7.4 --- Seller Curtailment**

If Seller voluntarily curtails generation from the Facility for any reason other than in response to a Curtailment Order or a curtailment instruction from Buyer (including but not limited to selling or diverting Energy on the spot market or to a third party), Seller shall pay to Buyer liquidated damages equal to one hundred twenty percent (120%) of the Contract Price for each MWh of Deemed Generated Energy that was curtailed, diverted, or otherwise not delivered to the Delivery Point. Such liquidated damages shall be in addition to any other remedies available to Buyer under this Agreement, including without limitation the right to terminate this Agreement pursuant to Section 15.1 if such curtailment or diversion constitutes a material breach of Seller\'s obligations hereunder.

**Section 7.5 --- Calculation of Deemed Generated Energy**

\(a\) Deemed Generated Energy for any period of curtailment or reduced generation shall be calculated using the Facility\'s performance model, which shall incorporate actual solar irradiance data recorded by the Facility\'s on-site pyranometers and weather stations during the relevant period.

\(b\) The performance model shall take into account the Facility\'s historical performance characteristics, including the DC/AC ratio, inverter clipping, transformer losses, soiling losses, and other balance-of-system losses, as well as the applicable Degradation Rate.

\(c\) Deemed Generated Energy shall be adjusted to exclude any periods of scheduled maintenance that were planned and notified to Buyer at least five (5) Business Days in advance.

\(d\) In the event of a dispute regarding the calculation of Deemed Generated Energy, either Party may engage an independent third-party engineer, mutually agreed upon by the Parties, to verify the calculation. The cost of such independent verification shall be borne by the Party whose calculation is determined to be less accurate.

\(a\) In addition to the Contract Price payable for Solar Energy and Discharged Energy under Section 8.1, Buyer shall pay to Seller a monthly BESS Capacity Payment of Five Dollars and Seventy-Five Cents (\$5.75) per kW-month, multiplied by the BESS Contract Capacity of 75,000 kW.

\(b\) The monthly BESS Capacity Payment shall equal: \$5.75 × 75,000 = \$431,250 per month.

\(c\) The annual BESS Capacity Payment shall equal: \$431,250 × 12 = \$5,175,000 per year.

\(d\) The BESS Capacity Payment is a fixed amount and shall remain unchanged for the entirety of the Delivery Term. No escalation, adjustment, index, or other modification of any kind shall apply to the BESS Capacity Payment at any time during the Delivery Term. The Parties acknowledge that the fixed nature of the BESS Capacity Payment was a material element of the commercial negotiation of this Agreement and was reflected in the pricing and other terms agreed upon by the Parties.

\(e\) The BESS Capacity Payment shall be payable regardless of actual BESS dispatch levels, provided that the BESS maintains a minimum Availability of ninety percent (90%) on a rolling thirty (30)-Day basis (measured pursuant to Section 7.3(b)(i)). If the Availability of the BESS falls below ninety percent (90%) in any calendar month, the BESS Capacity Payment for that month shall be prorated based on actual Availability (e.g., if Availability is 85%, the BESS Capacity Payment for such month shall equal \$431,250 × (85/90) = \$407,292).

**Section 8.3 --- BESS Energy Price**

Energy discharged from the BESS and delivered to the Delivery Point (\"Discharged Energy\") shall be settled at the Contract Price applicable to Solar Energy under Section 8.1 for the relevant Contract Year. For the avoidance of doubt, Discharged Energy shall not be settled at, and neither Party shall have any obligation based upon, the ERCOT real-time or day-ahead market settlement prices. The Contract Price for Discharged Energy is included within the overall bundled pricing structure of this Agreement.

**Section 8.4 --- Invoicing and Payment**

\(a\) Seller shall issue monthly invoices to Buyer within fifteen (15) Business Days following the end of each calendar month. Each invoice shall set forth in reasonable detail the following line items:

> \(i\) Total MWh of Solar Energy delivered to the Delivery Point during the invoice month;
>
> \(ii\) Total MWh of Discharged Energy delivered to the Delivery Point during the invoice month;
>
> \(iii\) The applicable Contract Price per MWh;
>
> \(iv\) The monthly BESS Capacity Payment;
>
> \(v\) Any Ancillary Services revenue sharing amounts due to Buyer or creditable against Seller\'s invoice pursuant to Section 7.3(c);
>
> \(vi\) Any curtailment compensation owed by Buyer pursuant to Section 7.1 or any Shortfall Liquidated Damages, Seller Curtailment liquidated damages, or other liquidated damages payable by Seller under this Agreement;
>
> \(vii\) Any Congestion Sharing amounts due from Seller pursuant to Section 8.5; and
>
> \(viii\) The net amount due from Buyer to Seller (or from Seller to Buyer, as the case may be).

\(b\) Buyer shall pay all undisputed amounts set forth on each invoice within twenty (20) Business Days following receipt of such invoice by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Seller.

\(c\) Interest shall accrue on any undisputed amounts not paid when due at a rate equal to the lower of (i) one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month and (ii) the maximum rate permitted by applicable Law.

\(d\) If Buyer disputes any amount set forth on an invoice, Buyer shall pay all undisputed amounts when due and shall provide Seller with written notice of the disputed amount, specifying the reasons for the dispute, within the twenty (20) Business Day payment period. Disputed amounts shall be resolved through the dispute resolution mechanism set forth in Article 22.

**Section 8.5 --- Congestion Risk Allocation**

\(a\) **General Allocation.** Buyer shall bear the Congestion Costs associated with the transmission of Energy from the Delivery Point (ERCOT Settlement Point LZ*WEST) to Buyer\'s Load Zone (ERCOT Load Zone LZ*SOUTH). Seller shall have no responsibility for Congestion Costs, subject to subparagraphs (b) and (c) below.

\(b\) **Congestion Cap.** If the annual average Congestion Cost, calculated as the total Congestion Costs incurred by Buyer in connection with Energy purchased under this Agreement during a Contract Year divided by the total MWh of Energy delivered to the Delivery Point during such Contract Year, exceeds Eight Dollars (\$8.00) per MWh (the \"Congestion Cap\"), Seller shall reimburse Buyer for fifty percent (50%) of the aggregate Congestion Costs in excess of the Congestion Cap for such Contract Year, subject to the Congestion Sharing Cap set forth in Section 8.5(c).

\(c\) **Congestion Sharing Cap.** Seller\'s aggregate reimbursement obligation under Section 8.5(b) shall not exceed Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$2,500,000) in any Contract Year (the \"Congestion Sharing Cap\"). In no event shall Seller\'s total payments under this Section 8.5 exceed the Congestion Sharing Cap in any Contract Year, regardless of the magnitude of actual Congestion Costs.

\(d\) **Calculation and Settlement.** Congestion Costs shall be determined monthly based on ERCOT settlement data and the actual metered deliveries during each settlement interval. Any reimbursement due from Seller under Section 8.5(b) shall be calculated on an annual basis at the end of each Contract Year and shall be reflected as a credit on Seller\'s invoice for the first calendar month following the conclusion of such Contract Year. If the Contract Year-end adjustment results in an amount due from Seller to Buyer that exceeds the amounts otherwise payable by Buyer to Seller on such invoice, the excess shall be paid by Seller to Buyer as an adjustment on the next following monthly invoice.

\(e\) **Example.** If the annual average Congestion Cost for a Contract Year is \$12.00 per MWh and the total Energy delivered to the Delivery Point during such Contract Year is 612,500 MWh, then: (i) the excess Congestion Cost above the Congestion Cap equals \$12.00 -- \$8.00 = \$4.00 per MWh; (ii) the total excess Congestion Cost equals \$4.00 × 612,500 MWh = \$2,450,000; (iii) Seller\'s share of excess Congestion Cost equals 50% × \$2,450,000 = \$1,225,000 (which is below the Congestion Sharing Cap of \$2,500,000, and therefore Seller would reimburse Buyer \$1,225,000 for such Contract Year).

For purposes of this Section 9.4(a), a change shall be deemed \"material\" if the Net Present Value of the Tax Credit reduction, calculated using a discount rate of seven and one-half percent (7.5%) per annum over the remaining Delivery Term, exceeds Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000).

\(b\) **Favorable Tax Change.** If, after the Effective Date, the federal Investment Tax Credit or Production Tax Credit benefits available to the Facility are materially increased, enhanced, or otherwise favorably modified as a result of a Change in Law (a \"Favorable Tax Change\"), Buyer may deliver a written notice to Seller requesting a reopener negotiation of the Contract Price to reflect the economic impact of such Favorable Tax Change. For purposes of this Section 9.4(b), the same materiality threshold set forth in Section 9.4(a) shall apply.

\(c\) Upon receipt of a notice under Section 9.4(a) or Section 9.4(b), the Parties shall negotiate in good faith for a period of ninety (90) days to agree upon a revised Contract Price that restores the economic balance of this Agreement as it existed immediately prior to the applicable Adverse Tax Change or Favorable Tax Change.

\(d\) If the Parties are unable to agree on a revised Contract Price within the ninety (90)-day negotiation period, either Party may submit the dispute to binding arbitration under Section 22.3 for determination of the appropriate Contract Price adjustment.

\(e\) During the pendency of any negotiation or arbitration under this Section 9.4, the existing Contract Price shall remain in effect, and all other terms and conditions of this Agreement shall continue unchanged and in full force and effect.

**Section 16.4 --- Mutual Termination**

This Agreement may be terminated at any time by the mutual written agreement of the Parties, upon such terms and conditions as the Parties may agree.

**Section 16.5 --- Buyer Regulatory Termination Right**

\(a\) **Trigger.** If, as a result of any Change in Law or change in ERCOT Protocols or ERCOT market rules occurring after the Amended and Restated Date, Buyer\'s All-In Cost of the Product purchased under this Agreement exceeds one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the then-prevailing ERCOT Wholesale Market Price (as determined by the average of the day-ahead and real-time settlement prices at the ERCOT Settlement Point LZ_SOUTH, weighted by Buyer\'s hourly load profile, over the applicable measurement period) for a period of twelve (12) consecutive months (a \"Regulatory Cost Event\"), Buyer shall have the right to terminate this Agreement upon one hundred eighty (180) days\' prior written notice to Seller. Buyer\'s termination notice shall include a detailed calculation demonstrating that the All-In Cost has exceeded the 150% threshold for twelve consecutive months, including supporting data from ERCOT settlement records.

\(b\) **Termination Payment.** In the event of termination by Buyer pursuant to this Section 16.5, Buyer shall pay to Seller a Termination Payment equal to the lesser of:

> \(i\) Fifty percent (50%) of the Net Present Value of the remaining Contract Price payments that would have been payable by Buyer over the remainder of the Delivery Term, calculated by assuming delivery of the Expected Annual Generation (as adjusted for degradation pursuant to Section 6.8) in each remaining Contract Year at the Contract Price applicable to each such remaining Contract Year (including the escalation set forth in Section 8.1(b) for Contract Years 11--20), and discounted at a rate of seven and one-half percent (7.5%) per annum from each future payment date back to the effective date of termination; or
>
> \(ii\) Thirty Million Dollars (\$30,000,000).

\(c\) The Termination Payment shall be due and payable within sixty (60) days following the effective date of termination (i.e., the date that is 180 days after the delivery of Buyer\'s termination notice).

\(d\) Payment of the Termination Payment by Buyer shall be Buyer\'s sole financial obligation to Seller in connection with a termination under this Section 16.5, and such payment shall constitute full and final settlement of any and all claims, losses, damages, costs, or liabilities of either Party arising from or in connection with such termination.

\(e\) For the avoidance of doubt, a change in ERCOT market prices alone, absent a Change in Law or a change in ERCOT Protocols or ERCOT market rules, shall not constitute a Regulatory Cost Event and shall not give rise to a termination right under this Section 16.5.

**Section 16.6 --- Effects of Termination**

Upon the expiration or earlier termination of this Agreement:

\(a\) All obligations of the Parties under this Agreement shall cease and terminate, except for those obligations that expressly survive termination in accordance with Section 2.2;

\(b\) Each Party shall pay to the other Party all amounts accrued and owing through the effective date of termination, including any unpaid invoices, liquidated damages, or other amounts due;

\(c\) Seller shall transfer to Buyer\'s designated ERCOT account all Renewable Energy Certificates for Energy generated prior to the effective date of termination that have not yet been transferred;

\(d\) All Performance Security (including Letters of Credit) shall be returned to the posting Party (less any amounts drawn) within sixty (60) days following the effective date of termination; and

\(e\) The Parties\' confidentiality obligations under Article 20 shall survive termination in accordance with Section 2.2.

**[ARTICLE 17 --- FORCE MAJEURE]{.underline}**

**Section 17.1 --- Definition**

\"Force Majeure\" means any event or circumstance that (x) is beyond the reasonable control of the Party claiming Force Majeure (the \"Affected Party\"), (y) was not caused by the negligence, fault, or willful misconduct of the Affected Party, and (z) prevents or materially impairs the Affected Party\'s ability to perform one or more of its material obligations under this Agreement, including the following events or circumstances:

\(a\) Acts of God, including lightning, earthquakes, and tsunamis;

\(b\) War (whether declared or undeclared), armed conflict, invasion, terrorism, insurrection, civil unrest, riots, or sabotage;

\(c\) Epidemics, pandemics, or quarantine restrictions imposed by a Governmental Authority;

\(d\) Strikes, lockouts, or labor disputes, except those involving the Affected Party\'s own employees or the employees of the Affected Party\'s contractors or subcontractors;

\(e\) Actions of Governmental Authorities, including the issuance of new or amended permits, injunctions, restraining orders, or ERCOT directives (subject, in the case of Curtailment Orders, to the System Curtailment Threshold set forth in Section 7.2);

\(f\) Earthquakes of magnitude 5.0 or greater on the Richter scale occurring within one hundred (100) miles of the Facility;

\(g\) Named tropical storms, hurricanes, or tornadoes occurring within twenty-five (25) miles of the Facility; and

\(h\) Fire, explosion, or flood (only if such flood is designated a federal disaster area by the Federal Emergency Management Agency or a successor agency).

**Exclusions.** Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following events and circumstances shall expressly not constitute Force Majeure under this Agreement:

> \(i\) Changes in market prices, including ERCOT real-time settlement prices, day-ahead settlement prices, or Locational Marginal Prices at any ERCOT Settlement Point;
>
> \(ii\) Seller\'s inability to obtain, maintain, or refinance financing for the Facility, including project-level debt, tax equity, or any other form of financing;
>
> \(iii\) Equipment, component, or material supply chain delays, shortages, or unavailability occurring after the Commercial Operation Date, including delays in the procurement of replacement parts, modules, inverters, batteries, or other Facility components;
>
> \(iv\) Weather events that do not meet the threshold of a named tropical storm, hurricane, or tornado occurring within twenty-five (25) miles of the Facility, including but not limited to hailstorms, ice storms, severe thunderstorms, dust storms, extreme heat events, or flooding that has not been designated a federal disaster area;
>
> \(v\) Changes in federal, state, or local tax law or tax credit availability (which are addressed exclusively under Section 9.4 of this Agreement); and
>
> \(vi\) Curtailment of the Facility\'s generation by ERCOT or any Transmission Service Provider in excess of the System Curtailment Threshold of five hundred (500) hours per Contract Year (which is addressed exclusively under Section 7.2 of this Agreement and shall not constitute Force Majeure for any purpose under this Agreement).

**Section 17.2 --- Notice and Mitigation**

The Affected Party shall provide written notice to the other Party within five (5) Business Days of the commencement of a Force Majeure event, which notice shall describe in reasonable detail (a) the nature of the Force Majeure event, (b) the anticipated duration of the event, (c) the specific obligations under this Agreement that the Affected Party is unable to perform as a result of the event, and (d) the actions being taken or planned by the Affected Party to mitigate the effects of the event. The Affected Party shall provide updated notices as circumstances change. The Affected Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate and minimize the effects of the Force Majeure event on its obligations under this Agreement and shall resume performance as soon as practicable following the cessation of the Force Majeure event.

**Section 17.3 --- Effect of Force Majeure**

The performance obligations of the Affected Party shall be suspended during the period in which a Force Majeure event prevents performance, subject to the limitations set forth in Section 7.2 with respect to ERCOT-directed curtailment. Neither Party shall be liable to the other Party for any failure or delay in performance attributable to a Force Majeure event, and such failure or delay shall not constitute an Event of Default under Article 15. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Force Majeure shall not excuse (a) any payment obligation that accrued prior to the occurrence of the Force Majeure event, or (b) any obligation to pay liquidated damages for periods prior to the commencement of the Force Majeure event. A Force Majeure event shall not extend the Delivery Term.

**[ARTICLE 18 --- INSURANCE]{.underline}**

**Section 18.1 --- Seller Insurance Obligations**

Seller shall obtain and maintain in full force and effect throughout the Delivery Term, at Seller\'s sole cost and expense, the following insurance coverages:

\(a\) **Commercial General Liability Insurance** with a minimum coverage limit of Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000) per occurrence and Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000) in the annual aggregate, including coverage for bodily injury, property damage, personal injury, advertising injury, contractual liability, and products/completed operations;

\(b\) **All-Risk Property Insurance** covering the Facility (including the BESS and all associated equipment) for one hundred percent (100%) of full replacement value, including coverage for wind, hail, flood, earthquake (if commercially available at reasonable cost), and electrical and mechanical breakdown;

\(c\) **Business Interruption Insurance** covering eighteen (18) months of lost revenue, calculated based on the Expected Annual Generation (as adjusted for degradation) multiplied by the then-applicable Contract Price, plus the annual BESS Capacity Payments;

\(d\) **Pollution Legal Liability Insurance** with a minimum coverage limit of Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000) per claim and in the aggregate, including coverage for gradual and sudden pollution events;

\(e\) **Workers\' Compensation Insurance** as required by the laws of the State of Texas, including employer\'s liability coverage with a minimum limit of One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000);

\(f\) **Automobile Liability Insurance** with a minimum combined single limit of Two Million Dollars (\$2,000,000), including coverage for hired and non-owned vehicles; and

\(g\) **Umbrella/Excess Liability Insurance** with a minimum coverage limit of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000), providing excess coverage over the commercial general liability, automobile liability, and employer\'s liability policies.

Detailed insurance requirements, including deductible limitations and special endorsements, are set forth in Schedule C.

**Section 18.2 --- Additional Insured**

Buyer (Brazos Valley Municipal Power Agency) and its officers, directors, employees, agents, and member cities shall be named as additional insureds on all insurance policies required under Sections 18.1(a), (b), (c), (d), and (g). Seller shall provide Buyer with certificates of insurance evidencing all required coverages within thirty (30) days of policy inception and within thirty (30) days of each policy renewal. Seller shall provide Buyer with at least thirty (30) days\' advance written notice (or ten (10) days in the case of non-payment of premium) of any cancellation, non-renewal, or material modification of any required insurance policy.

**Section 18.3 --- Self-Insurance**

Seller may not self-insure any coverage required under Section 18.1 without the prior written consent of Buyer, which consent may be withheld in Buyer\'s sole discretion.

**[ARTICLE 19 --- INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**

**Section 19.1 --- Seller Indemnification**

Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Buyer and its officers, directors, employees, agents, representatives, and member cities (collectively, the \"Buyer Indemnitees\") from and against any and all third-party claims, actions, suits, demands, judgments, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and court costs) arising from or in connection with:

\(a\) Any breach by Seller of any representation, warranty, covenant, or obligation under this Agreement;

\(b\) The negligence, gross negligence, or willful misconduct of Seller, its employees, agents, contractors, or subcontractors in connection with the construction, operation, or maintenance of the Facility;

\(c\) Any personal injury, death, or property damage occurring at or emanating from the Facility, to the extent caused by or attributable to the acts or omissions of Seller, its employees, agents, contractors, or subcontractors; and

\(d\) Any environmental contamination, remediation liability, or environmental compliance costs arising from or caused by Seller\'s activities at the Facility site.

**Section 19.2 --- Buyer Indemnification**

Buyer shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Seller and its officers, managers, members, employees, agents, and representatives (collectively, the \"Seller Indemnitees\") from and against any and all third-party claims, actions, suits, demands, judgments, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and court costs) arising from or in connection with any breach by Buyer of this Agreement, or the negligence, gross negligence, or willful misconduct of Buyer, its employees, agents, or contractors in connection with Buyer\'s activities at or beyond the Delivery Point.

**Section 19.3 --- Indemnification Procedures**

\(a\) The Party seeking indemnification (the \"Indemnified Party\") shall provide the indemnifying Party (the \"Indemnifying Party\") with prompt written notice of any claim or action for which indemnification is sought, and in any event within fifteen (15) Business Days of becoming aware of such claim or action. Failure to provide timely notice shall not relieve the Indemnifying Party of its indemnification obligations except to the extent that the Indemnifying Party is materially prejudiced by such failure.

\(b\) The Indemnifying Party shall have the right to assume the defense and control of any such claim or action, at its sole cost and expense, with counsel reasonably acceptable to the Indemnified Party.

\(c\) The Indemnifying Party shall not settle any claim without the prior written consent of the Indemnified Party (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld) if such settlement would impose any obligation, restriction, or liability on the Indemnified Party.

\(d\) The Indemnified Party shall cooperate in good faith with the Indemnifying Party in the defense of any claim, at the Indemnifying Party\'s expense.

The Receiving Party shall not disclose Confidential Information to any Person, except as follows:

\(a\) To the Receiving Party\'s Affiliates, officers, directors, employees, advisors (including legal counsel, accountants, and financial advisors), and lenders, in each case who have a need to know such information and who are bound by confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in this Section;

\(b\) As required by applicable Law, regulation, court order, subpoena, or the rules of a securities exchange; provided that the Receiving Party shall, to the extent permitted by Law, provide the Disclosing Party with prompt notice of such required disclosure and cooperate with the Disclosing Party in seeking a protective order;

**[ARTICLE 22 --- DISPUTE RESOLUTION]{.underline}**

**Section 22.1 --- Senior Executive Negotiation**

If a dispute arises under or in connection with this Agreement, the Parties shall first attempt to resolve such dispute through direct negotiation between their respective designated senior executives. Seller\'s designated senior executive shall be the Chief Executive Officer of Seller\'s Parent, Meridian Renewable Holdings LLC (currently David Chadwick). Buyer\'s designated senior executive shall be the General Manager of Buyer (currently Robert Fuentes). The senior executives shall meet (in person or by videoconference) within fifteen (15) Business Days after one Party delivers written notice to the other Party requesting senior executive negotiation, and shall negotiate in good faith for a period of thirty (30) days from the date of their initial meeting to resolve the dispute.

**Section 22.2 --- Mediation**

If the dispute is not resolved through senior executive negotiation within the thirty (30)-day period set forth in Section 22.1, either Party may submit the dispute to non-binding mediation administered by the Texas Energy Mediation Panel or, if such panel is unavailable, by the American Arbitration Association. The mediation shall take place in Austin, Texas. The Parties shall select a mutually agreeable mediator within fifteen (15) days of the mediation request. If the Parties cannot agree on a mediator, the administering organization shall appoint one. The mediation shall conclude within sixty (60) days of the mediator\'s appointment, unless the Parties agree in writing to extend such period. Each Party shall bear its own costs and attorneys\' fees in connection with the mediation, and the Parties shall equally share the mediator\'s fees and the costs of the mediation facility.

**Section 22.3 --- Binding Arbitration**

If the dispute is not resolved through mediation within the time period specified in Section 22.2, either Party may submit the dispute to final and binding arbitration under the Commercial Arbitration Rules of the American Arbitration Association (\"AAA\"). The arbitration shall be conducted in Houston, Texas before a panel of three (3) arbitrators. Each Party shall select one (1) arbitrator within fifteen (15) days of the demand for arbitration, and the two (2) Party-appointed arbitrators shall select the third arbitrator (who shall serve as chair of the tribunal) within fifteen (15) days of their appointment. Each arbitrator shall have expertise in the electric power industry or energy law. The arbitrators shall issue a reasoned written award within one hundred twenty (120) days following the conclusion of the arbitration hearing. The arbitration award shall be final and binding upon the Parties, and judgment on the award may be entered in any court of competent jurisdiction. The prevailing Party in the arbitration shall be entitled to recover its reasonable attorneys\' fees and costs from the non-prevailing Party.

**Section 22.4 --- Governing Law**

The Parties consent to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in Harris County, Texas for any proceedings seeking to enforce an arbitration award or for any proceedings not subject to the arbitration provisions of this Article 22.

**Section 22.5 --- Provisional Remedies**

**[ARTICLE 23 --- MISCELLANEOUS]{.underline}**

There are no side letters, amendments, supplements, or other written or oral agreements between the Parties modifying, supplementing, or otherwise affecting the terms of this Amended and Restated Agreement as of the date hereof.

**Section 23.2 --- Amendments**

No amendment, modification, or supplement to this Agreement shall be effective unless set forth in a written instrument executed by both Parties.

**Section 23.3 --- Waiver**

No waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall be effective unless set forth in a written instrument executed by the Party waiving such provision. The failure of either Party to enforce any provision of this Agreement at any time shall not be deemed a waiver of such provision or of the right to enforce such provision at any subsequent time. No single or partial exercise of any right or remedy shall preclude any other or further exercise thereof.

**Section 23.4 --- Severability**

If any provision of this Agreement is held by a court or arbitral tribunal of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect any other provision of this Agreement, and the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect. The Parties shall negotiate in good faith to replace any invalid or unenforceable provision with a valid and enforceable provision that achieves, to the greatest extent possible, the economic, business, and other purposes of the original provision.

**Section 23.5 --- No Third-Party Beneficiaries**

This Agreement is entered into for the sole benefit of the Parties and their respective permitted successors and assigns, and nothing in this Agreement shall confer upon any lender, financing party, investor, member city, or other third party any rights, remedies, obligations, or causes of action under this Agreement, except as may be expressly provided in a separate consent and agreement entered into among Seller, Buyer, and an applicable lender or financing party pursuant to Section 14.3.

**Section 23.6 --- Counterparts**

This Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Execution and delivery of this Agreement by electronic signature (including PDF) shall be valid and effective for all purposes.

**Section 23.7 --- Further Assurances**

Each Party shall execute and deliver such further documents, instruments, and agreements, and take such further actions, as may be reasonably necessary or appropriate to carry out the purposes and intent of this Agreement and to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby.

doc.add_heading("1. Executive Summary — Bottom Line for the Investment Committee", level=1)
para("The PPA is a 20-year (COD March 15, 2023 to March 14, 2043), unit-contingent, physically-settled, bundled (energy + RECs) offtake with an A2/A-rated Texas municipal power agency, plus a fixed BESS capacity payment. Contracted revenue is approximately **$20.2 million in Contract Year 1** ($15.0M energy at $24.50/MWh on 612,500 MWh P50 + $5.175M BESS capacity), and approximately **$363.6 million nominal over Contract Years 3–20** (our P50 calculation, degraded per Section 6.8). The revenue core is sound and largely market-standard. However, several provisions are off-market and adverse to the Seller (and therefore to Alder Creek as acquirer), and at least two issues are transaction-critical:")
bullet("**Change of Control consent is required for this acquisition (Sections 1.1, 14.2(b)–(d)).** The sale of 100% of Seller\u2019s membership interests is a \"Change of Control\" requiring BVMPA\u2019s prior written consent. BVMPA may withhold consent if the acquirer/credit support provider is rated below BBB-. Deemed consent arises only 45 Business Days after a complete information package. A non-consented closing exposes the PPA to a Seller Event of Default and termination. **Consent (plus an estoppel) must be a closing condition.**")
bullet("**Latent tax-credit price reopener in Buyer\u2019s favor (Section 9.4(b)).** The Favorable Tax Change test runs from the Effective Date (September 1, 2021). The Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 (enacted August 16, 2022) materially enhanced ITC/PTC economics for solar and standalone storage after that date, and the A&R (January 18, 2023) did not carve it out or acknowledge it as priced in. BVMPA arguably retains a live right to demand renegotiation of the $24.50/MWh Contract Price, with binding arbitration if no agreement. There is no deadline for exercise. **This is potentially the largest single value risk; require a BVMPA estoppel/waiver or a seller indemnity / price protection.**")
bullet("**Buyer Regulatory Termination Right with capped payment (Section 16.5).** BVMPA may terminate on 180 days\u2019 notice if a Change in Law or ERCOT rule change drives its All-In Cost (which includes congestion) above 150% of LZ_SOUTH wholesale prices for 12 consecutive months. The Termination Payment is the lesser of 50% of the NPV (7.5%) of remaining energy payments (BESS payments excluded) and **$30 million** — against roughly $150M NPV of remaining energy payments today (50% = ~$75M), so the $30M cap binds until about Contract Year 17. Highly non-standard; a buyer option on the contract.")
bullet("**ERCOT curtailment risk sits with the Seller above 500 hours/year (Sections 7.2, 17.1(vi)), and the threshold is already being exceeded.** 620 hours occurred in Contract Year 1 and 410 hours through December 31, 2024 in Contract Year 2. Excess hours are not Force Majeure, are uncompensated and count against the Minimum Annual Delivery. Note the Technical Summary understates the revenue impact: **all ~14,500 MWh of Year 1 ERCOT-curtailed energy was unpaid (~$355,250)**, not just the ~2,900 MWh above the threshold ($71,050). The 500-hour Force Majeure treatment excuses delivery, not payment.")
bullet("**Seller bears a capped share of LZ_WEST\u2013LZ_SOUTH congestion (Section 8.5).** Seller reimburses 50% of average congestion above $8.00/MWh, capped at $2.5M per Contract Year (up to about 12% of Year 1 revenue; the cap is reached at about $16.16/MWh average congestion on P50 volumes). It is unusual for a physical-delivery seller to share buyer-side basis risk.")
bullet("**BESS economics are flat and carry an augmentation obligation.** $5.75/kW-month fixed for 20 years with no escalation (Section 8.2(d)) (about 38% real erosion by Year 20 at 2.5% inflation). Seller must maintain 270 MWh (90%) usable capacity for 15 years through augmentation (Schedule A), against a supplier warranty of only 70% retention at year 20. Seller also bears charging energy and round-trip losses. The Technical Summary does not mention the augmentation obligation; the model must include augmentation capex.")
bullet("**Liability architecture is off-market for a long-dated PPA.** There is no mark-to-market termination payment for Buyer default, and aggregate liability is capped at the lesser of 3 years\u2019 payments or $50M (Section 15.5), which effectively caps Seller\u2019s recovery for a BVMPA repudiation at about $50M against ~$200M NPV of remaining contracted revenue. There are no lender step-in/cure rights (Section 14.3).")
bullet("**Document integrity / disclosure discrepancies.** The copy provided shows blank signature lines despite being described as \"fully executed\". Schedule B fixes the Buyer Downgrade LC at **$9.5M** while Section 13.4(b) yields **$10,090,625** (and Section 13.4(d) defers to Schedule B). The Credit Summary cites $10.1M. Several Technical Summary data points diverge from Schedule A. Details are in Section 6.")
para("**Overall view:** The PPA supports an investment-grade contracted revenue profile. We recommend that the IC approve proceeding **subject to** (i) BVMPA Change of Control consent and estoppel as a condition precedent, (ii) resolution of the Section 9.4(b) IRA reopener exposure (BVMPA waiver/estoppel, or specific indemnity/escrow or price adjustment), (iii) the financial model reflecting the curtailment, congestion, BESS augmentation, flat capacity payment and Section 16.5 termination downside cases, and (iv) the confirmatory diligence items in Section 8.")

ts("G. Congestion Risk Allocation", [
 ["General Allocation","Buyer bears Congestion Costs (positive or negative) from LZ_WEST to LZ_SOUTH (8.5(a); 5.2).","Market","Consistent with physical delivery at the Seller’s settlement point."],
 ["Seller Sharing","If annual average Congestion Cost exceeds $8.00/MWh (Congestion Cap), Seller reimburses 50% of the excess, capped at $2.5M per Contract Year (Congestion Sharing Cap). Settled annually as a credit on the first invoice after CY-end (8.5(b)–(e)).","Non-Standard (Adverse)","Shifts buyer-side basis risk back to Seller. On P50 volumes, the cap is reached at ~$16.16/MWh average congestion. The maximum exposure is $2.5M/yr (~12% of CY1 revenue). It is unclear whether the Section 15.5 aggregate liability cap applies to these payments. Congestion also counts in Buyer’s All-In Cost for the 16.5 termination test."],
])
ts("H. Tax Credits and Change in Law", [
 ["Tax Credit Ownership","Seller owns all ITC/PTC (Code §§48/45 and successors). The Contract Price reflects Seller’s expectation of Tax Credits. Buyer covenants not to impair the credits and indemnifies Seller for breach (9.1–9.2; 1.1 \"Tax Credits\").","Market","Customary. Confirm which credit was claimed (ITC vs PTC), any transferability (§6418) or tax equity structure, and recapture period status. The ITC recapture period runs 5 years from placed-in-service (to ~2028), which is relevant to a change in ownership of a partnership."],
 ["Change in Law (general)","Each Party bears its own Change in Law costs (including ERCOT protocol changes) except 9.4 and 16.5. Change in Law is not an excuse except to the extent it is Force Majeure (9.3).","Market","Customary allocation, but asymmetric in practice because 16.5 gives Buyer an exit for regulatory cost increases while Seller has no equivalent right."],
 ["Tax Credit Reopener","Two-way: Seller (Adverse Tax Change) or Buyer (Favorable Tax Change) may request repricing if the change after the Effective Date has NPV impact > $5M (7.5% discount). 90-day good-faith negotiation, then binding AAA arbitration (22.3) to \"restore the economic balance\". The existing price applies pending resolution. No exercise deadline (9.4(a)–(e)).","Non-Standard (Adverse)","Tax reopeners are uncommon in operating-asset PPAs. The baseline date (Sept. 1, 2021) precedes the IRA, so BVMPA has a credible argument that IRA enhancements (ITC to 30% base plus potential adders; standalone storage ITC; PTC option for solar) are a Favorable Tax Change. Arbitral repricing risk is open-ended for the life of the contract. This is our highest-priority value diligence item."],
])
ts("I. Environmental Attributes", [
 ["Ownership / Transfer","All Environmental Attributes (including future attributes) belong to Buyer at no extra cost. Seller registers with ERCOT REC program and transfers RECs within 30 days after month-end, at Seller’s cost (10.1–10.3).","Market","Customary bundled structure. Drafting gap: the definition of Environmental Attributes (\"any attribute created by federal... governmental action\") does not expressly exclude Tax Credits. 9.1 should control, but an express carve-out is market and should be confirmed in the estoppel. RECs on grid-charged Discharged Energy are not addressed."],
])
ts("J. Credit Support", [
 ["Seller Performance Security (post-COD)","$7.5M LC from COD, stepping down to $5.0M on March 15, 2028 if no Seller EoD is continuing. Issuer must be a Qualified Institution (≥ A- Crestline; ≥ $10B assets). Replacement within 30 BD of issuer downgrade (13.2; Schedule B §I).","Market","Roughly $30/kW AC, within the customary operating-period range. At closing, Alder Creek must replace Meridian-sponsored LC credit support without a gap (15.1(d): failure to maintain for 30 BD after notice is an EoD). Pre-COD LCs ($20M / $15M) are spent (13.1)."],
 ["Buyer Credit Support","No collateral while Investment Grade. Reliance on A2/A Crestline rating and rate-setting authority (13.3; 11.2(f)).","Market","Typical for highly-rated public power. Note that \"Investment Grade\" is Baa3 from Crestline, and the ratings are from a single agency (Crestline) only."],
 ["Buyer Downgrade Event","Trigger: rating falls below Baa2/BBB. Buyer posts an LC equal to 6 months’ estimated payments within 30 BD. Formula in 13.4(b) yields $10,090,625 (CY1), but 13.4(d) says the amount \"is as set forth in Schedule B\", which states $9,500,000. LC is released after 12 months back at or above Baa2/BBB. Failure to post is a Buyer EoD (13.4; 15.2(e); Schedule B §II).","Ambiguous","The trigger one notch above the IG floor is favorable. However, the conflict between the formula and Schedule B is unresolved, and 13.4(d) likely makes the lower $9.5M amount control, which is fixed and does not track escalation (the formula gives ~$10.7M by CY20). The Credit Summary’s $10.1M is therefore not reliable. Clarify in the estoppel."],
 ["LC Mechanics","Irrevocable; Schedule D form; 1-year evergreen with 60-day non-renewal notice (draw in full on non-renewal); sight draft + certificate; ISP98 or UCP 600 at issuer’s election; partial draws; NY-law LC form (13.5; Schedules B §III, D).","Market","Customary."],
])
ts("K. Assignment, Change of Control and Financing", [
 ["Change of Control (definition)","More than 50% direct or indirect transfer of equity of Seller or Seller’s Parent; merger where holders retain < 50%; or any change in the ultimate controlling parent (1.1).","Market","Captures the proposed 100% acquisition and any future upstream transfers by Alder Creek (exit planning)."],
 ["Change of Control / Non-Affiliate Assignment","Requires Buyer’s prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. Buyer may withhold if the assignee (or its parent guarantor/credit support provider) is rated below BBB- or had a bankruptcy or similar proceeding within 7 years. Information package required (org chart, ratings, financials, transaction description, O&M capability). Buyer has 45 Business Days after a complete package; silence is deemed consent (14.2(b)–(d)).","Non-Standard (Adverse)","Many investor-friendly PPAs permit Change of Control without consent to \"qualified transferees\" meeting rating or experience tests. Here consent is required, and the safe harbour for refusal is broad. Assignment without consent is void (14.1), and a CoC without consent is likely a material breach (15.1(b)). Deemed consent mitigates hold-up risk, but the clock runs only from a complete package. Treat as a gating item."],
 ["Affiliate Assignment","Permitted without consent if Seller or Seller’s Parent guarantees the assignee and gives notice within 15 BD (14.2(a)).","Market","Useful for post-closing internal restructuring, subject to a parent guaranty."],
 ["Collateral Assignment / Lender Protections","Seller may collaterally assign rights (not obligations) to lenders without consent, with notice within 15 BD. No lender step-in, cure rights or consent obligations; a separate consent is to be \"negotiated in good faith\" on request (14.3; 23.5).","Non-Standard (Adverse)","Financing PPAs typically include an obligation to execute a customary lender consent (with cure periods and step-in). Absence may affect acquisition financing, back-leverage or tax equity terms."],
 ["Buyer Assignment","Buyer may assign without consent to a successor Texas municipal power agency or a successor to substantially all assets, if the assignee is Investment Grade (≥ Baa3); otherwise Seller consent is required, not to be unreasonably withheld (14.4).","Market","Customary. The Investment Grade floor (Baa3) is lower than the Buyer Downgrade trigger (Baa2/BBB), so an assignee rated Baa3 would immediately owe an LC."],
])
ts("L. Events of Default, Remedies and Liability", [
 ["Seller EoDs","Payment default (10 BD after notice); material breach (60-day cure, extendable to 120 days); failure to maintain Performance Security (30 BD after notice); Insolvency Event; FM > 365 consecutive days (15.1). COD default is spent (15.1(c)).","Market","Cure periods are reasonable. Note that there is no express EoD for persistent MAD shortfall (LDs only) or for failing the 270 MWh BESS capacity, but either could be argued as material breach."],
 ["Buyer EoDs","Payment default (10 BD after notice); material breach (60/120 days); Insolvency Event; FM > 365 days; failure to post the Downgrade LC (15.2).","Market","Customary."],
 ["Remedies","Non-defaulting Party may suspend payments (payment defaults only), draw security, terminate on 30 days’ notice (immediately for insolvency) and pursue law/equity remedies subject to 15.5. Remedies are cumulative (15.4; 16.1).","Non-Standard (Adverse)","There is no defined termination payment or mark-to-market settlement amount on Buyer default. **PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION / ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT**

*Contains Confidential Information subject to PPA Article 20 and the Mutual Confidentiality Agreement dated November 15, 2024 (Meridian Renewable Holdings LLC / Alder Creek Capital Partners LP)*

**MEMORANDUM**

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **To:**                             Investment Committee, Alder Creek Capital Partners LP (attn: James Whitford)
  ----------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **From:**                           Stonebridge Hart --- Nathan Gould and deal team

  **For:**                            Investment Committee meeting of February 10, 2025

  **Re:**                             Project Lone Star --- Amended and Restated Power Purchase Agreement between Lone Star Solar Project LLC (Seller) and Brazos Valley Municipal Power Agency (Buyer): Structured Term Sheet Summary and Market-Standard / Non-Standard Assessment
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*Documents reviewed: (1) Amended and Restated Power Purchase Agreement dated January 18, 2023 (original effective date September 1, 2021), including Schedules A--D (the \"PPA\"); (2) BVMPA Counterparty Credit Summary prepared by Meridian Finance (January 2025) (the \"Credit Summary\"); (3) Lone Star Solar Project Technical Summary prepared by Meridian Engineering, Doc. Ref. MRH-LSSP-TS-2025-001 (January 2025) (the \"Technical Summary\"); and (4) transmittal email from Catherine Yeung (Whitfield & Crane, Seller counsel) dated January 27, 2025. Section references are to the PPA unless stated otherwise. The Meridian materials are expressly provided without representation or warranty; where they conflict with the PPA, the PPA controls and we flag the conflict.*

# 1. Executive Summary --- Bottom Line for the Investment Committee

The PPA is a 20-year (COD March 15, 2023 to March 14, 2043), unit-contingent, physically-settled, bundled (energy + RECs) offtake with an A2/A-rated Texas municipal power agency, plus a fixed BESS capacity payment. Contracted revenue is approximately **\$20.2 million in Contract Year 1** (\$15.0M energy at \$24.50/MWh on 612,500 MWh P50 + \$5.175M BESS capacity), and approximately **\$363.6 million nominal over Contract Years 3--20** (our P50 calculation, degraded per Section 6.8). The revenue core is sound and largely market-standard. However, several provisions are off-market and adverse to the Seller (and therefore to Alder Creek as acquirer), and at least two issues are transaction-critical:

- **Change of Control consent is required for this acquisition (Sections 1.1, 14.2(b)--(d)).** The sale of 100% of Seller's membership interests is a \"Change of Control\" requiring BVMPA's prior written consent. BVMPA may withhold consent if the acquirer/credit support provider is rated below BBB-. Deemed consent arises only 45 Business Days after a complete information package. A non-consented closing exposes the PPA to a Seller Event of Default and termination. **Consent (plus an estoppel) must be a closing condition.**

- **Latent tax-credit price reopener in Buyer's favor (Section 9.4(b)).** The Favorable Tax Change test runs from the Effective Date (September 1, 2021). The Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 (enacted August 16, 2022) materially enhanced ITC/PTC economics for solar and standalone storage after that date, and the A&R (January 18, 2023) did not carve it out or acknowledge it as priced in. BVMPA arguably retains a live right to demand renegotiation of the \$24.50/MWh Contract Price, with binding arbitration if no agreement. There is no deadline for exercise. **This is potentially the largest single value risk; require a BVMPA estoppel/waiver or a seller indemnity / price protection.**

- **Buyer Regulatory Termination Right with capped payment (Section 16.5).** BVMPA may terminate on 180 days' notice if a Change in Law or ERCOT rule change drives its All-In Cost (which includes congestion) above 150% of LZ_SOUTH wholesale prices for 12 consecutive months. The Termination Payment is the lesser of 50% of the NPV (7.5%) of remaining energy payments (BESS payments excluded) and **\$30 million** --- against roughly \$150M NPV of remaining energy payments today (50% = \~\$75M), so the \$30M cap binds until about Contract Year 17. Highly non-standard; a buyer option on the contract.

- **ERCOT curtailment risk sits with the Seller above 500 hours/year (Sections 7.2, 17.1(vi)), and the threshold is already being exceeded.** 620 hours occurred in Contract Year 1 and 410 hours through December 31, 2024 in Contract Year 2. Excess hours are not Force Majeure, are uncompensated and count against the Minimum Annual Delivery. Note the Technical Summary understates the revenue impact: **all \~14,500 MWh of Year 1 ERCOT-curtailed energy was unpaid (\~\$355,250)**, not just the \~2,900 MWh above the threshold (\$71,050). The 500-hour Force Majeure treatment excuses delivery, not payment.

- **Seller bears a capped share of LZ_WEST--LZ_SOUTH congestion (Section 8.5).** Seller reimburses 50% of average congestion above \$8.00/MWh, capped at \$2.5M per Contract Year (up to about 12% of Year 1 revenue; the cap is reached at about \$16.16/MWh average congestion on P50 volumes). It is unusual for a physical-delivery seller to share buyer-side basis risk.

- **BESS economics are flat and carry an augmentation obligation.** \$5.75/kW-month fixed for 20 years with no escalation (Section 8.2(d)) (about 38% real erosion by Year 20 at 2.5% inflation). Seller must maintain 270 MWh (90%) usable capacity for 15 years through augmentation (Schedule A), against a supplier warranty of only 70% retention at year 20. Seller also bears charging energy and round-trip losses. The Technical Summary does not mention the augmentation obligation; the model must include augmentation capex.

- **Liability architecture is off-market for a long-dated PPA.** There is no mark-to-market termination payment for Buyer default, and aggregate liability is capped at the lesser of 3 years' payments or \$50M (Section 15.5), which effectively caps Seller's recovery for a BVMPA repudiation at about \$50M against \~\$200M NPV of remaining contracted revenue. There are no lender step-in/cure rights (Section 14.3).

- **Document integrity / disclosure discrepancies.** The copy provided shows blank signature lines despite being described as \"fully executed\". Schedule B fixes the Buyer Downgrade LC at **\$9.5M** while Section 13.4(b) yields **\$10,090,625** (and Section 13.4(d) defers to Schedule B). The Credit Summary cites \$10.1M. Several Technical Summary data points diverge from Schedule A. Details are in Section 6.

**Overall view:** The PPA supports an investment-grade contracted revenue profile. We recommend that the IC approve proceeding **subject to** (i) BVMPA Change of Control consent and estoppel as a condition precedent, (ii) resolution of the Section 9.4(b) IRA reopener exposure (BVMPA waiver/estoppel, or specific indemnity/escrow or price adjustment), (iii) the financial model reflecting the curtailment, congestion, BESS augmentation, flat capacity payment and Section 16.5 termination downside cases, and (iv) the confirmatory diligence items in Section 8.

# 2. Key Issues Dashboard (Ranked)

*Severity reflects our view of value or transaction risk to Alder Creek as acquirer of 100% of Seller. \"Market\" assessments are qualitative and based on our general experience with utility-scale ERCOT solar and solar-plus-storage offtake agreements; they are not benchmarked against a proprietary dataset.*

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **\#**      **Issue**                                                                                                  **PPA Ref.**                                            **Severity**   **Why It Matters**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    **Recommended Action**
  ----------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------- -------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1           Change of Control requires BVMPA consent; BBB- credit test; 45 BD deemed consent                           1.1 (Change of Control); 14.1; 14.2(b)--(d); 15.1(b)    High           Closing without consent risks a void transfer or material-breach Event of Default (60/120-day cure) and termination. Alder Creek (fund) is likely unrated; an \"unrated\" acquirer is arguably not \"below BBB-\", but BVMPA will likely demand a rated guarantor or LC. Timing: a complete package delivered mid-February 2025 implies deemed consent no earlier than about mid-to-late April 2025.                                                  Make BVMPA written consent plus estoppel a CP to closing. Submit the 14.2(c) package early. Pre-structure credit support (parent guaranty from a rated entity or an incremental LC). Align the PSA outside date with the 45 BD clock.

  2           IRA-driven Favorable Tax Change reopener available to BVMPA                                                9.4(b)--(e); 1.1 (Change in Law, Effective Date)        High           Measured \"after the Effective Date\" (Sept. 1, 2021). The IRA (Aug. 16, 2022) increased ITC/PTC value and created standalone storage ITC. The \$5M NPV materiality threshold is very likely exceeded on a facility of this size. A successful reopener reduces the Contract Price for the remaining term via negotiation then binding arbitration. There is no exercise deadline. The A&R recitals do not record that IRA benefits were priced in.   Obtain BVMPA estoppel/waiver that no Favorable Tax Change claim exists for the IRA. Alternatively obtain a Meridian special indemnity (survival to term), escrow or purchase price adjustment. Obtain the Original Agreement and the A&R negotiation history (Thomas Berwick) and the tax credit election/placed-in-service records.

  3           Buyer Regulatory Termination Right; Termination Payment capped at \$30M                                    16.5; 1.1 (All-In Cost; ERCOT Wholesale Market Price)   High           A buyer option to exit on regulatory-driven cost increases. The All-In Cost includes congestion and ERCOT charges. The ERCOT market design is in active flux. The payment is about \$30M versus \~\$75M (50% NPV) uncapped and \~\$200M NPV of total remaining contracted revenue (energy + BESS). The \"as a result of\" causation standard is untested and susceptible to dispute.                                                                  Model a termination downside case. Seek BVMPA estoppel that no Regulatory Cost Event is pending. Consider pricing/structure protection (e.g., R&W or special indemnity is unlikely to cover; reflect in price). Consider merchant tail value post-termination.

  4           ERCOT curtailment above 500 hrs/yr at Seller risk and counted against MAD; threshold already exceeded      7.2; 17.1(e), (vi); 6.2                                 High           620 hrs in CY1; 410 hrs through 12/31/24 in CY2. The trend is increasing as LZ_WEST solar builds out. All ERCOT-curtailed MWh are unpaid (within or above 500 hrs). Above 500 hrs, curtailed MWh also count as shortfall for MAD/Shortfall LDs. The current MAD cushion is large (CY1 actual 602,300 MWh vs 490,000 MAD), so near-term LD risk is low but revenue erosion is ongoing.                                                                 Independent engineer curtailment forecast (nodal study at Pecos 345 kV). Model curtailment sensitivities. Seek seller price protection for CY2 actuals. Diligence ERCOT/TSP planned transmission upgrades.

  5           Seller share of LZ_WEST--LZ_SOUTH congestion                                                               8.5; 5.2                                                Med            50% above \$8.00/MWh average, capped at \$2.5M per Contract Year (max \~\$45M nominal over CY3--20). Historical West--South basis volatility makes this a live exposure, and congestion also feeds Buyer's All-In Cost test under 16.5.                                                                                                                                                                                                               Obtain historical LZ_WEST--LZ_SOUTH basis data and any amounts reimbursed/invoiced in CY1--CY2. Model the cap as a downside case.

  6           BESS: flat \$5.75/kW-mo for 20 years; 270 MWh capacity maintenance for 15 years; charging cost on Seller   8.2; 7.3(e); Schedule A §5                              Med            No escalation (real erosion). Augmentation capex is required to keep 90% usable capacity through Year 15 (supplier warranty: 70% at Year 20). Seller supplies charging energy (solar or grid) and absorbs \~13% round-trip losses; Discharged Energy is paid only at the \$24.50 Contract Price.                                                                                                                                                      IE review of augmentation plan/capex reserve and BESS warranty/LTSA. Confirm the model includes augmentation, charging costs and RTE losses.

OK: output/ppa-term-sheet-summary.docx valid

- **BVMPA estoppel certificate** confirming: the PPA is in full force with no amendments, side letters or waivers; no defaults or disputes; no Favorable Tax Change notice and (ideally) a waiver of any 9.4(b) claim relating to the IRA; no Regulatory Cost Event or 16.5 notice; curtailment hours and Free Curtailment volumes by Contract Year; any congestion reimbursement owed; current LC amounts (Seller \$7.5M; Buyer Downgrade LC = \$9.5M or the formula amount); and treatment of Buyer-curtailed energy for MAD purposes.

- **Lender consent agreement** (14.3), if acquisition financing or back-leverage is contemplated, negotiated alongside the CoC consent.

- **Replacement credit support** at closing for the \$7.5M Seller LC (and any parent guaranty BVMPA requires as a consent condition), arranged so there is no lapse under 15.1(d).

## 8.2 Purchase agreement protections

- A specific indemnity (surviving to the end of the Delivery Term or the reopener exposure period), escrow or price adjustment for any 9.4(b) Contract Price reduction attributable to tax law changes enacted before closing (including the IRA).

- Reps on: an executed and complete PPA; no amendments/side letters/waivers; no notices of default, FM, Regulatory Cost Event or Tax Reopener; accuracy of curtailment and invoicing data; compliance with the Schedule C insurance program (including the \$500k property deductible cap); BESS capacity ≥ 270 MWh and the status of augmentation; tax credit claims and recapture position.

- Address ITC recapture and tax-equity/transfer consequences of the acquisition with tax counsel (the Facility was placed in service in 2023, so the recapture period runs to \~2028).

- Covenant to cooperate with BVMPA consent, plus an outside date sized to the 45-Business-Day clock.

## 8.3 Confirmatory diligence / model inputs

- IE nodal curtailment and congestion study (Pecos 345 kV / LZ_WEST--LZ_SOUTH), including planned transmission upgrades. Obtain CY1--CY2 settlement, invoice and congestion data.

- BESS: augmentation plan and capex, LTSA/warranty terms, charging cost and RTE assumptions, AS revenue actually shared (40%) to date.

- Tax: ITC vs PTC election, credit amount, any §6418 transfer or tax equity, and the A&R negotiation record on IRA pricing (Thomas Berwick / Whitfield & Crane).

- BVMPA: multi-agency ratings, audited financials, rate covenant, member-city contract tenors, Uri impacts, immunity and Chapter 9 analysis by Texas public-power counsel.

- Technical reconciliation of the Schedule A vs. Technical Summary discrepancies (site area, inverters, modules).

- Model downside cases for the 16.5 termination (\$30M payment then merchant), flat BESS payment, congestion at the cap, and elevated curtailment.

# 9. Scope, Assumptions and Limitations

- This summary is based solely on the four documents listed above. We have not reviewed the Original Agreement, interconnection agreement, ground lease, EPC/O&M/BESS supply contracts, tax credit documentation, insurance certificates, or ERCOT settlement data.

- Market-standard characterizations are qualitative judgments for IC orientation and should not be read as a statistical benchmark. Federal tax and Texas public-law points are flagged for confirmation by tax and Texas counsel.

- Financial figures are our arithmetic from PPA formulas at P50, without curtailment, congestion, AS revenue or availability adjustments. NPVs use a 7.5% discount rate (the PPA rate) and a mid-year convention.

- The Credit Summary and Technical Summary were prepared by Seller's Parent and are expressly not representations or warranties. Figures drawn from them have not been independently verified.
